pĕnārĭus , a, um, adj. penus,
I.of or for provisions: “cella,” Cic. Sen. 16, 56 ; id. Verr. 2, 2, 2, § 5.—Subst.: pĕnārĭa , ae, a storehouse: a celando cellam appellarunt; “penariam, ubi penus,” Varr. L. L. 5, § 162 Müll.; also, pĕnārĭus , i, m., a storehouse, granary: penora dicuntur res necessariae ad victum cotidianum, et locus eorum penarius, Paul. ex Fest. p. 211 Müll.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
